The '''2024 Adur District Council election''' was held on Thursday 2 May 2024, alongside the [[2024 UK local elections|other local elections being held in the United Kingdom]] on the same day.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Election dates to Worthing and Adur Councils |url=https://www.adur-worthing.gov.uk/elections-and-voting/upcoming-elections/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240104162511/https://www.adur-worthing.gov.uk/elections-and-voting/upcoming-elections/ |archive-date=4 Jan 2024 |access-date=4 Jan 2024 |website=Adur and Worthing Councils}}</ref> The councillors elected will serve a 4-year term, ending in May 2028.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Composition of Adur District Council |url=http://opencouncildata.co.uk/council.php?c=165&y=0 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240104162909/http://opencouncildata.co.uk/council.php?c=165&y=0 |archive-date=4 Jan 2024 |access-date=4 Jan 2024 |website=Open Council Data UK}}</ref>

== Background ==
[[Adur District Council]] elects half of its councillors every 2 years, with 16 being up for election this time, being 15 ordinary elections plus a by-election in St Mary's ward.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Dale |first1=Bob |title=Four Sussex council areas prepare to vote in local elections |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-sussex-68278782 |access-date=18 April 2024 |work=BBC News |date=12 April 2024}}</ref><ref name=":0" />

Prior to the election, the council was under [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative]] majority control, although they only had a two-seat majority and the council was identified as a target for [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite news |title=Adur result - Local Elections 2022 |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/election/2022/england/councils/E07000223 |access-date=2024-01-04 |work=BBC News |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Green |first=Daniel |date=2024-04-14 |title=Adur local elections: How a red wave can end 25-year Tory grip on south coast |url=https://labourlist.org/2024/04/labour-local-elections-2024-adur-district-council/ |access-date=2024-04-24 |website=LabourList |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==Summary==
The election saw Labour win an outright majority for the first time in the council's history.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Morton |first1=Sam |title=Local elections 2024: Labour take control of Adur council for first time ever; Worthing retained |url=https://www.sussexexpress.co.uk/news/politics/council/local-elections-2024-labour-take-control-over-adur-council-for-first-time-ever-worthing-retained-4616126 |access-date=24 July 2024 |work=Sussex World |date=3 May 2024}}</ref> Labour group leader Jeremy Gardner was formally appointed as leader of the council at the subsequent annual council meeting on 23 May 2024.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Hanway |first1=Thomas |title=Adur council's new chairman and leader take up roles |url=https://www.sussexexpress.co.uk/news/politics/council/adur-councils-new-chairman-and-leader-take-up-roles-4642308 |access-date=24 July 2024 |work=Sussex World |date=24 May 2024}}</ref>
